title: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument PSSA ship reporting system (CORAL SHIPREP), North-western Hawaiian Islands
authority: United States Coast Guard Communication Area Master Station Pacific (CAMSPAC) as shore-based authority; reports go to NOAA (nwhi.notifications@noaa.gov)
applies_to: Ships of 300 gross tonnage or more in transit through the reporting area that are entering or leaving a United States port or place (condition of port entry), and all such ships in a developing emergency. Sovereign immune ships exempt. Other ships of 300 GT or more, fishing vessels and all ships in an emergency are recommended to report. US-flag vessels must report under US law.
applies_quote: As a condition of entry to a United States port or place, all ships 300 gross tonnage or greater, and all ships in the event of a developing emergency, and that are in transit through the reporting area are required to participate in CORAL SHIPREP, except for sovereign immune vessels which are exempt under SOLAS regulation V/1. (MSC.248(83), Annex, para 1.1.1)

when.text: Each ship should submit a full report in accordance with paragraph 3.2.1 as soon as it crosses the boundary to enter the ship reporting system. (para 3.3.1; for ships that must report, should is to be read as shall)
Each ship should submit a report in accordance with paragraph 3.2.2 as soon as it crosses the boundary to leave the ship reporting system. (para 3.3.2)
Further reports should be made whenever there is a change in navigation status or circumstances, particularly in relation to item Q of the reporting format. (para 3.3.3)

how.note: Primary: send by Inmarsat-C (or ship's email) as a direct email; NOAA pays Inmarsat-C costs (50 CFR 404 Appendix E). Do not use batch message routing services. Address from 50 CFR 404.4(d), (e). MSC.279(85) prints it as "nwhi.notifications@noaa-gov", an obvious misprint; the US rule and the 2007 text use @noaa.gov.
In a developing emergency, to request response and assistance (MSC.248(83) para 5.2). Number as printed in 2007; not re-confirmed.
For US vessels under 300 GT without email (50 CFR 404.4(f)).
For US vessels under 300 GT without email (50 CFR 404.4(f)).

heading: CORAL SHIPREP //

lines.text: Ship: vessel name/call sign/flag/IMO number/Federal documentation or State registration number if applicable // (e.g. A/OCEAN VOYAGER/C5FU8/BAHAMAS/IMO 9359165//)
Date, time (UTC), and month of entry: a 6-digit group (day, hours, minutes) suffixed by Z and three letters for the month // (e.g. B/271107Z DEC//)
Position: 4-digit latitude group with N, a single /, and 5-digit longitude group with W // in WGS-84 (e.g. C/2728N/17356W//)
Speed in knots and tenths: 3-digit group indicating knots decimal tenths // (e.g. F/20.5//)
Destination and estimated time of arrival: name of port city/country/estimated arrival date and time group as in B // (e.g. I/SEATTLE/USA/311230Z DEC//)

Intended route through the reporting area: a direct rhumb line (RL) course and intended speed, or a series of waypoints (WP) with speed between them; as many L lines as needed // (e.g. L/RL/215/20.5// or L/WP/2734N/17352W/20.5//)
Vessel draft in meters: maximum present static draft in meters decimal centimeters // (e.g. O/11.50//)
Categories of hazardous cargoes: classification code (e.g. IMDG, IBC, IGC, INF) / all corresponding categories, comma separated // (e.g. P/IMDG/1.4G,2.1,2.2,2.3,3,4.1,6.1,8,9//)
Defects or deficiencies: brief details of defects, damage, deficiencies or limitations that restrict maneuverability or impair normal navigation // (if none, enter the number zero)
Pollution incident or goods lost overboard within the Monument, the Reporting Area, or the U.S. EEZ // (if none, enter the number zero) (e.g. R/0//)
Contact information of ship's agent or owner: name/address/and phone number //
Ship size (length overall and gross tonnage) and type: LOA in meters decimal centimeters/gross tons/type of ship // (e.g. U/294.14/54592/CONTAINER SHIP//)
Persons: total number of persons on board // (e.g. W/15//)

format_note: Lines above are the ENTRY report (50 CFR 404 Appendix E, table E.1; the IMO list in MSC.248(83) para 3.2.1 is A, B, C or D, E or F, I, L, O, P, Q or R, T, U, W). The EXIT report is CORAL SHIPREP //, A, B (date, time and month of exit), C and R (Appendix E table E.3; IMO para 3.2.2 lists A, B, C or D). The automatic system rejects reports that do not follow the exact format: no extra text, extraneous characters or double spacing. Hazardous cargo details may be sent by non-verbal means before entering. Language English.

(19) 27° 26´.10 N, 178° 32´.23 W; Then an arc with a 60.17 nm radius centred at (20) 28° 25´.23 N, 178° 19´.51 W; Then to point (1) 29° 24´.21 N, 178° 06´.45 W. Inner Boundary. (MSC.279(85), Annex, para 2)

verification: Outer boundary points 1 to 19 and the arc centres 20 and 21 read from MSC.279(85) Annex para 2 (IMO PDF pages 2 and 3) by pdftotext and a regex, then re-read by eye against the page. Arc points (9a1 to 9a7, 19a1 to 19a7) were computed on a sphere at the printed radius; the printed end points lie 60.2 NM from their centres, which confirms the radius. Who must report from MSC.248(83) para 1; address, report syntax and exit report from 50 CFR 404.4 and Appendix E (eCFR, 2026-10-01).
notes: The reporting area is the band between the outer boundary and the Areas To Be Avoided (ATBA): you report when you cross the outer boundary inward and again when you cross it outward. The ATBA circles and connecting areas (listed in area_quote) are the inner limit and must be avoided anyway. Two parts of the outer boundary are arcs, not straight lines: points 9 to 10 (round Nihoa, east end) and 19 to 1 (round Kure, west end); the points named 9a1 to 9a7 and 19a1 to 19a7 are computed along those arcs only to draw them and are flagged inferred. Discrepancy: the US regulation 50 CFR 404 Appendix D still lists the original 2007 outer boundary of MSC.248(83) (100 points, slightly different, e.g. point 1 29 25.47N 178 16.97W), while IMO replaced it in MSC.279(85) (in force 1 June 2009). This record follows the IMO text; the difference is small (about 1 to 10 NM). The Monument was enlarged in 2016 and became a National Marine Sanctuary in 2025; those larger limits are NOT the reporting area. The IMO title calls it a ship reporting system; it is mandatory only for the ships in applies_to (via US port entry conditions) and recommended for others.
